text:
alex.support: Heads-up — ACME reported a sudden ~320ms P99 increase for API calls from ap-south-1 at 2026-07-12T09:12Z. They included a trace showing an unexpected hop to us-west-2. Escalating to SRE/networking.

ingrid-obs: Link to trace? Can you paste the trace id and a quick snippet of the hop list?

alex.support: Trace ID: trc_20260712_acme_9. Full trace: https://obs.redwood/traces/trc_20260712_acme_9 . Snippet from the trace span list: 
```
0: client -> edge-ap-south-1 (12ms)
1: edge-ap-south-1 -> border-egress-01 (18ms)
2: border-egress-01 -> usw2-peering-5 (210ms)
3: usw2-peering-5 -> origin-dedicated-1 (320ms)
```

maria-sre: That jump at hop 2 -> 3 looks like an egress rewrite to our us-west peering node. Did a change roll yesterday to routing policies? @james-platform any config pushes?

james-platform: I pushed a small egress fallback tweak to routing rules at 2026-07-11T22:40Z to prefer lower-cost peerings for non-SLA accounts. It should respect region affinity - investigating now.

netbot: alert: route-policy-change detected by config-audit at 2026-07-11T22:40:17Z (author: james-platform). Affected services: api-proxy, border-egress.

maria-sre: Can someone run an internal traceroute from edge-ap-south-1 to a known ACME origin IP to reproduce? Use the internal probe: `infra probe trace --from edge-ap-south-1 --to 10.45.128.9 --capture-hops`

james-platform: Running now... pastebin: https://paste.redwood/tmp/trace-out.txt 
Trace result: 
```
edge-ap-south-1 -> border-egress-01 (15ms)
border-egress-01 -> route-rewrite-lb (18ms)
route-rewrite-lb -> usw2-peering-5 (215ms)
usw2-peering-5 -> origin-dedicated-1 (305ms)
```

nina-cs: ACME says spike started ~09:10Z and affects only a subset of requests - looks like some requests still hit ap-south egress normally.

maria-sre: That suggests policy is mis-evaluating for a subset (likely based on account tier header or missing region affinity tag). Can we dump the policy decision logs for a sample request id? @alex.support can you pull X-Request-Id from ACME's failing call?

alex.support: Example failing request id: req_ak47_20260712_091205. Attached full request headers in the trace. Header of interest: `x-customer-tier: pro` and `x-region-preference: ap-south-1`

james-platform: I pulled the policy decision trace for that req. Decision tree: 
- match customer-tier != enterprise -> apply cost-priority fallback
- fallback route selected: peer-usw2 (score 0.4) despite `x-region-preference` being present due to a bug in header parsing when header order changes. I'm opening PR to fix header parsing.

maria-sre: Immediate mitigation: revert the cost-priority fallback roll or update fast gate to exclude requests with `x-region-preference`. Which is faster?

james-platform: Reverting the rule on the config service will take ~2 minutes to deploy. Patching gate to short-circuit on x-region-preference will take ~20m with a canary. I'll revert now and follow with patch.

ops-bot: deploy started: configs-service revert (change id cfg_20260712_revert) by james-platform.

netbot: routing metrics: border-egress-01 -> usw2-peering-5 traffic drops by 78% within 90s of revert. p99 for ACME returns to baseline ~28s after revert.

maria-sre: Nice. Root cause: header-parsing bug meant region-preference header was ignored for some header orders, so fallback policy routed some traffic cross-region. Action items: (1) james -> revert done + patch PR #4321 to fix header parsing, (2) platform -> add a unit test for header order permutations, (3) ops -> add alert for sudden cross-region hop when trace shows >1 cross-region egress in 5m, (4) product -> communicate to CS what happened.

james-platform: Revert completed and verified. PR #4321 opened: https://code.redwood/pulls/4321 (includes unit + integration tests). I'll follow up with canary for patch later today.

nina-cs: I'll update ACME: explain we had a mis-eval of routing header ordering, rollback completed, performance restored, and we'll follow up with a postmortem.

alex.support: Thanks all. Saving traces/links in the ticket. Will file a short postmortem draft after the patch lands. :thumbsup:

maria-sre: Please include repro steps in the PM: command to reproduce trace, sample headers, and trace id. Also add suggested long-term guardrails (policy simulation + route-affinity unit tests).

alex.support: Will do. Closing the escalation after PM draft.
